title: Deep Origin and BioAge score early win in AI drug hunt
source_used: Deep Origin press release (via Yahoo Finance, GlobeNewswire)
key_facts: Deep Origin and BioAge Labs (Nasdaq: BIOA) announced a multi-target AI-driven drug discovery collaboration on 14 Oct 2026.
Deep Origin's software found small-molecule hits against a novel BioAge target in under three months; BioAge validated them in its own wet lab.
BioAge is moving its first target into hit-to-lead optimization and will test more targets.
Deep Origin is eligible for success-based milestone payments.
Deep Origin cites an August 2026 bioRxiv preprint with a 30.6% hit rate on one target (CD73), about 100 times a previously published machine-learning screen.
BioAge develops drugs for cardiometabolic diseases by targeting the biology of human aging.
quote_evidence: The collaboration has reached its first milestone: novel small-molecule hits identified computationally by Deep Origin against a novel BioAge target have been validated in BioAge's wet lab.
As part of the collaboration with BioAge, Deep Origin's platform delivered multiple structurally distinct hits against the first target in less than three months.
why_it_matters_hint: A lab-confirmed hit is only an early step; the real test is whether a drug follows.
notes: Read the company's paid press release, not FirstWord Pharma's article (blocked, empty text). All claims are company statements.
